News.title: Cop who took naked selfies of her ‘work boobies’ in stab vest & offered to give a ‘helping hand’ on duty is sacked
News.content:
RAUNCHY ROZZER Cop who took naked selfies of her ‘work boobies’ in stab vest & offered to give a ‘helping hand’ on duty is sacked

A WOMAN cop who took naked selfies of her “work boobies” while in uniform in a police station cupboard was sacked for gross misconduct.

PC Alisha Staves, 31, snuck into an office storeroom at a cop shop and took a topless snap of herself wearing a police fleece jacket.





She then sent it to her partner with the message: “Maybe Mrs Officer can give you a helping hand.”

In the second selfie, taken at home, she posed semi-naked to partially show off her boobs while wearing a police stab vest.

Staves, who worked in the firearms licensing department for Humberside Police, also sent this image onto her partner with the message: “Work boobies”.



The images, taken in 2023, were discovered on her private phone two years later during a download of her electronic devices in an unrelated investigation.

At the time she was the subject of an unspecified written warning.

After the cheeky snaps were discovered Staves was charged with gross misconduct.

Andrew Pickin, representing Humberside Police, said she had taken the snaps after her partner expressed doubts that she was a front line cop.



He said her behaviour was “of a sexual nature” and went “beyond poor judgment”.

Pickin added that her actions amounted to a serious abuse of her position and harmed the force’s reputation.

He continued: “There is little difficulty in concluding that this sort of deliberate and completely inappropriate behaviour is so serious as to justify dismissal.

“The officer evidently has no issues in taking revealing photos of herself, wearing items of police uniform, and sending these on.”

Matthew Baron, representing Staves, who joined the force in 2019 and was based at a station in Hull, said: “It was a mistake.



“She was being pressured by her partner who was teasing her about not being a real police officer.

“There was a degree of trying to make a bit of a joke about it.

“She accepts it was a poor decision, particularly the second one being taken on police premises.

“It was her honest belief they would never be shared further or be put in the public domain as has now happened as evidence in this case.”

Mr Baron added that she was confident that no-one would have walked into the storeroom while she was taking the semi-naked selfie as everyone had left for the day.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Chief Constable Chris Todd said Staves had committed a clear breach of professional standards which amounted to gross misconduct.

She was dismissed with immediate effect.

News.title: Pensioner dubbed ‘Granny Canute’ has clifftop home demolished AGAIN… 13 years after she had another house ripped down
News.content:
LIVING ON THE EDGE Pensioner dubbed ‘Granny Canute’ has clifftop home demolished AGAIN… 13 years after she had another house ripped down

A PENSIONER dubbed Granny Canute had her clifftop home demolished today, 13 years after her previous house was ripped down for the same reason.

Bulldozers have arrived in the erosion-hit village of Happisburgh, Norfolk, to demolish Bryony Nierop-Reading’s home and two others.





Mrs Nierop-Reading, 79, has lived on the eroding coastline since 2009, and witnessed the demolition of the Old Coastguard House today.

She first moved into a 1930s, three-bedroom bungalow on Beach Road which she bought for £25,000.

The property was around 20ft from the sea at the time, perched atop an 80ft cliff.

As her idyllic sea views became closer, the extension on the home was left hanging over the edge.

The devastated pensioner watched as her dream home was demolished in 2013, just two weeks before Christmas after a tidal surge left her bungalow wrecked.

Her neighbours moved out one-by-one, but defiant Bryony refused to leave – even when she was offered £53,000 under a Government compensation scheme.

Mrs Nierop-Reading said: “It has been a long, ongoing process which has made it more difficult because it has just dragged on and on.”



The grandmother was given the nickname ‘Granny Canute’ after refusing to move away from the cliffs.

She moved into a static caravan in her garden last year, which she will continue to live in as she continues to fight to save the village.

She moved into a static caravan that was lifted into her back garden using an 80 tonne crane last February.

Her neighbour Nicola Bayless’ house is also being demolished over the next few days.

It has been her family home for the last 26 years, with her parents first buying it in 2000 and then she moved in in 2016.



Speaking today, Nicola said: “It is heart-breaking.”

Her late parents, Anita and Arthur Richmond, originally bought Beacon House in 2001 when it was over 670ft (200m) away from the cliff’s edge.

Rob Goodliffe, coastal manager at NNDC, said: “It is a sad day for everybody.

“It is not something anybody wants to see but hopefully it has provided the owners of these properties to be able to move on in their different ways.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

King Canute, who ruled England between 995 and 1035, is said to have tried to turn back the tide – but failed as the waves began lapping around his feet.



But historians say this is just a myth and, in fact, the Saxon monarch was really trying to show to courtiers that despite his powers he wasn’t great enough to stop the sea.

News.title: Evil killer laughed and bragged ‘I stabbed him fully’ after slaughtering student on railway tracks
News.content:
MONSTER’S SMILE Evil killer laughed and bragged ‘I stabbed him fully’ after slaughtering student on railway tracks

AN EVIL murderer laughed and bragged “I stabbed him fully” after callously slaughtering a student on railway tracks.

Dino Donaldson, 21, was caught grinning on CCTV less than an hour after knifing Anojan Gnaneswaran to death at Strawberry Hill station in Twickenham.





The horror unfolded on January 8, 2024, when a row broke out on the platform between two groups of men over a drug deal involving £50 for 10 MDMA tablets.

The confrontation quickly spiralled into violence before Donaldson chased the 21-year-old accounting student onto the tracks.

He then stabbed him repeatedly in the chest, abdomen and thigh.

Mr Gnaneswaran was pronounced dead at the scene.



Shocking footage later showed Donaldson aboard an N87 night bus, smiling and laughing in the aftermath of the killing.

Even more chilling was audio captured on a doorbell camera, in which he boasted: “I stabbed him through the back bro, I stabbed him fully.

“I watched it and I felt it go in him, yeah.”

Donaldson was arrested three days later on January 11 at his home in West London.



Cops found him hiding in a cupboard in his property.

A search of his bedroom uncovered 74 wraps of crack and heroin with a street value of more than £1,000.

The victim’s devastated family paid tribute to a “much-loved son and brother”.

They said: “Anojan was in his third year at university studying accounting and finance, and he was so excited for his future.

“He excelled at all sports and had achieved first-dan black belt in karate – he competed in the World and European championships in karate, and we will all miss him so much.”



Following a trial at the Old Bailey, Donaldson, of Caxton Road, Ealing, was on Tuesday found guilty of murder by a unanimous jury.

Judge Angela Rafferty KC remanded him in custody and adjourned sentencing to a date to be fixed.

British Transport Police Detective Chief Inspector Paul Attwell hoped Donaldson’s sentence would provide “closure” to Mr Gnaneswaran’s family.

He said: “What started as an argument over a drug deal ended in a young man’s life being cut short by a remorseless thug.

“Donaldson showed his true colours as a coward by arming himself with a knife that night.



“His cowardice has continued by never accepting responsibility and admitting his crime – thankfully the jury saw through his lies.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“While no verdict can ever compensate for the loss of Anojan, I hope today’s outcome provides his family with some sense of closure.

“Thanks to our extensive investigation, justice has now been served to the man responsible for killing their loved one.”

News.title: Influencer slapped with jaw-dropping SIX-FIGURE fine – for feeding birds during boat trip with pals
News.content:
AN influencer has been hit with a six-figure fine after sharing a video of birds being fed BBQ meat during a boat trip.

Officials say Carlinhos Maia filmed two men chucking pieces of grilled beef to wild animals circling above the vessel.





The Brazilian social media star has been told to pay £150,000 by authorities who claim his actions constitute an environmental crime.

The clip, later posted to Maia’s social media accounts, was deemed serious enough for Brazil‘s environmental protection agency to issue the penalty.

Authorities said the men who physically fed the birds were fined separately, but Maia was punished for publishing and profiting from the footage.



Agency head, Lilian Hangae, said: “Carlinhos Maia was on a vessel with colleagues who fed birds barbecue, which is an environmental crime.

“The video was posted on social media. This is the reason for the violation.”

Officials added the amount was partly based on Maia’s huge online reach of 35 million followers.

The birds seen in the video were identified as magnificent frigatebirds.



This protected seabird species is common to the islands of Fernando de Noronha where the shocking footage was filmed.

Environmental authorities say feeding them beef is considered abusive because it is not part of their natural diet, harming their health.

It can even disrupt their behaviour, putting the ecological balance of the area out of sync.

Maia has since hit back online, branding the punishment “one of the biggest absurdities I’ve ever seen in my life.”

The influencer insisted that he did not personally feed the birds.



“I didn’t feed them. I accept a fine, no problem, but a fair fine,” he said.

“They are asking me for BRL 1 million because I posted a story of that moment.”

The influencer said his legal team is preparing to challenge the fine in court.

They will argue that similar cases on the island have only led to fines of around £750.

News.title: Astonishing moment rubbish truck tailgate opens to reveal SIXTY migrants crammed inside at border as armed cops aim guns
News.content:
THIS is the astonishing moment cops open a garbage truck to discover more than 60 Palestinian migrants stashed inside.

Dozens of men were bundled inside the truck with bags of trash, trying to escape the West Bank and cross into Israel.





Shocking footage showed the migrants crammed on top of one another and tumbling out of the truck whilst unknown liquids leaked from above.

The fleeing migrants were found during a routine inspection at the Cross-Shomron checkpoint.

Security forces swarmed the vehicle and pointed their firearms at the truck.



Slowly the rubbish truck lifted its tailgate compartment to reveal an unbelievable sight.

Dozens of men were tightly packed inside with the bags of rubbish.

Police arrested the driver at the scene.

He was an unnamed man in his 30s living in Israel.



Cops said he did not have the correct driving licence to drive the vehicle.

The Palestinians were on their way to “various cities inside the country”, officers said.

“But a joint operation by officers from the Judea and Samaria District and Border Police operating around Jerusalem thwarted the driver’s plan, and he was arrested”, they added.

The driver has been taken in for questioning and the migrants are in custody.

It’s not the first time desperate migrants have tried to cross from Palestine to Israeli territory using a bin lorry.



In 2024, The Jerusalem Post reported that 23 Palestinians were arrested, found hiding in the back of a similar vehicle.

Cops said the migrants were caught trying to cross the border at the Maccabim junction, near Jerusalem.

It comes as Greek authorities have been found to have their own measures to keep asylum seekers at bay.

Dramatic footage shows a gang of masked men running through a crowd of panicked migrants at the Greek land border near the Evros River.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In an investigation by the BBC, unearthed documents allegedly reveal that senior Greek officers have ordered and overseen the recruitment of the “migrant mercenaries” since 2020.



The mercenaries — hailing from countries including Pakistan, Syria and Afghanistan — are allegedly rewarded with cash and mobile phones, often looted from the migrants they’re pushing back.

News.title: We can’t defend Britain if you keep splurging on benefits, army of critics tell Starmer as forces starved of funding
News.content:
RAMPANT welfare spending is swallowing the funds needed to restore Britain’s cash-strapped military, Sir Keir Starmer was warned by an army of critics today.

Labour came under fire for rubber-stamping an extra 1.5million Universal Credit claims since the election – including 63,000 last month alone.





It means 8.4million people – a staggering one in eight of the entire population – are now receiving the main benefit payment.

Former Labour defence secretaries, top brass, and political rivals turned on the PM for letting welfare spending balloon while the armed forces are starved of funding.

His own adviser, the ex-NATO chief Lord George Robertson, blasted: “We cannot defend Britain with an ever-expanding welfare budget.”

Total welfare spending including pensions is this year expected to rise by £18billion to an eye-watering £332billion, which equals around 11 per cent of GDP.



It dwarfs the £62billion annual Ministry of Defence budget which is around 2.4 per cent of GDP.

Sir Keir has pledged to increase that to 3 per cent before the next election but is under pressure to accelerate that timeline amid increasing global conflict.

He is also facing accusations of dithering on the long-awaited Defence Investment Plan that was promised last summer but has been fought over by warring ministers.

Lord Robertson, who co-authored the government’s strategic defence review last year, accused the PM of “corrosive complacency”.



In a blistering intervention, Tony Blair’s former defence secretary said: “We are underprepared. We are underinsured.

“We are under attack. We are not safe… Britain’s national security and safety are in peril.”

His co-author General Sir Richard Barrons piled in: “It is a question of choices. If public expenditure is £1.3trillion they can find and extra £10 billion if they want to.

“But if you are the Chancellor you want to spend the money on other things. Defence is a second order priority and it will take us 10 years to get there.”

The Sun previously revealed the MoD is facing a £28billion black hole over the next four years.



Haggling between Defence Secretary John Healey and Chancellor Rachel Reeves has seen the investment plan delayed and with no end in sight.

Meanwhile Britain’s military has been left wanting during the Iran crisis, with much of our naval fleet undergoing repaits.

Another ex-Labour defence secretary, Lord John Hutton, also slammed the PM for failing to grip the benefits bill while military cash is needed.

He told Times Radio Labour has “been in office for a couple of years now, there’s no real sign that it’s got any agenda for correcting the very steep rise in welfare payments.”



Ms Reeves bottled a mere £5billion of welfare cuts last year following a rebellion by her MPs.

She has since commissioned a series of reviews into the welfare system, but has not committed to getting the total benefits bill system down.

Instead the bill is forecast to rise to more than £400billion, with extra increases from pension payments, health benefits and lifting the two-child benefit cap.

Asked about the growing number of people on handouts, she played down the scale of the issue.

She told Mumsnet: “In terms of this distinction between who’s on benefits and who’s not on benefits – well, most parents get child benefit. That’s a benefit… I think this sort of “people on benefits and people not on benefits” – it’s just not as simple as that.”

Labour’s welfare tsar Alan Milburn is looking into the issue of the million youngsters not in either employment nor training.



Today he warns that the issue of jobless white working class boys especially is a “national scandal” that must be tackled.

Shock figures reveal that nearly one in four, some 22.9 per cent, of white British young people are so-called NEET. This is higher than most comparable groups.

Research also shows that 30 per cent of NEET white young people indicate they have health conditions or disability – compared to 17 per cent of other ethnic groups combined.

Mr Milburn told The Sun: “A generation of white working-class boys are at particular risk of being left on the scrapheap.

“It is a national scandal. One in four disadvantaged white British youngsters are not in work, education or training – they’ve dropped out completely.



“If we truly believe in a fair Britain, we can’t keep looking the other way while our young are left behind.”

Slamming yesterday’s benefit stats, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said: “I agree completely with Lord Robertson. He is saying what I have been saying now for months, that Labour has become the welfare party. All they care about is welfare.”

Her Shadow Welfare Secretary Helen Whatley branded it a “full-blown crisis with a claim form attached.”

Former Tory Defence Secretary Grant Shapps told The Sun: “The first duty of any government is to defend the nation. At a time of rising global instability, that should be the clear priority.

“Yet Labour’s instincts take them in the wrong direction. They’re out of step with the vast majority of working people who expect their government to keep the country safe first and foremost.”



Lib Dem former soldier Mike Martin MP said: “We should be war ready yesterday but we have got an armed forces that can’t deploy.

“We have seen with HMS Dragon that we can’t get a ship to the Med on the turn of the handle. We can’t get a thousand troops to Europe.”

A UK Government spokesperson said: “We are delivering on the Strategic Defence Review to meet the threats we face.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It is backed by the largest sustained increase in defence spending since the Cold War, with a total of over £270 billion being invested across this Parliament.

“We are finalising our Defence Investment Plan that we will publish as soon as possible, putting the best kit and technology into the hands of our forces, rebuilding British industry to make defence an engine for growth and doubling down on our own commitment to NATO.”

News.title: Welcome to ‘Yellow Stone’… Travellers unveil name of 17-plot ‘illegal’ camp after paving over field in quiet village
News.content:
TRAVELLERS have unveiled the name of their 17-plot camp with fuming residents still battling to save their sleepy village.

Locals say unpermitted works had been carried out on the plot of land after 21 caravans and five mobile homes descended on the Surrey village nearly two weeks ago.





Residents in Alfold, Surrey, told of their despair after 30 to 40 grab lorries arrived in the quiet neighbourhood.

Now, a new influx of travellers has arrived at Alfold – spurring new building work and sparking fears that house prices may decrease by five figures.

A brand new sign at the site reads: “Yellow Stone Farm, 1-17.”



One person told MailOnline: “The whole situation is a massive slap in the face. It’s an almighty insult.

“They do what they want. They have even put up a sign which says Yellow Stone Farm. They have given themselves a name. It shows a complete lack of respect.”

Fresh building work continued until Friday afternoon, before an injunction was brought in making it illegal to carry on.

Another resident added people were “terrified” of the travellers and were concerned about what would happen next.



The local, known as Rosemary, said she was worried another group would arrive in another empty field.

She said there was another Bank Holiday coming up next month and there was an empty field opposite.

Rosemary added that the council had been “warned”.

Alfold locals first became alarmed on April 1 after spotting unknown men measuring the width of the road.

Their fears came to fruition just 24 hours later when up to 40 lorries armed with building supplies arrived to construct “gated community” on the rural field.



They were astonished to see the lorries unload pipes, wood, steel and other supplies to create a new 17-plot community.

Since then, works have reportedly continued around the clock adding 21 caravans and five mobile homes to the site.

Residents have described the occupation as an “almighty insult” and the injunction as “too little, too late”.

Furious locals said they were “incredibly angry ” and had been left feeling unsafe.

They claimed it was like a “military operation”.



Peter Foy, 52, who lives a five-minute-walk away from the site, claimed construction work had been taking place until the early hours of each morning – with lights from the site visible across the village.

The dad-of-two said that “all hell descended upon us” at around 4pm on Thursday afternoon when they turned it into a gated community with “great big steel doors”.

He recalled how there was a constant stream of “caravan after caravan and huge lorries”.

Locals initially reported the site to the police, but were told no criminal offences were identified.

Surrey Police said: “The development of the site is a planning permission issue, which is being led by Waverley Borough Council.”



Councillors also told of their frustrations with the site, which has gone ahead despite being issued two “stop notices” to try to force work to cease under the Town and Country Planning Act.

They said they were not aware the site would be used in this way and are reportedly monitoring the situation closely.

Jane Austin, the leader of the Waverley Conservative Council group told The Sun: Alfold residents feel powerless.

“How can it possibly be right that those who appear to knowingly break the law at scale seem to face no immediate consequences, while local people are left to watch their village field being tarmacked over?

“The temporary injunction is an important step because it means no further work can now take place, but the reality is that residents are still facing months of legal and planning action ahead.



“Residents should not have to watch their countryside destroyed while taxpayers are more than likely left to foot the clean-up bill.”

A statement from a spokesperson for Waverley Borough Council said: “Council officers visited the site on Thursday 2 April in the evening and again on Friday 3 April.

“We are aware that further works were carried out over the Easter weekend.

“Temporary Stop Notices were served on Thursday 2 April and again on Friday 3 April, however, these have not been complied with.

“The Council has now secured an Interim Injunction from the High Court.



“This means that nothing further can be brought on to the land.

“To date, six of the plots have mobile homes sited on them; the rest of the plots have touring caravans.

“Further action will follow to secure the reversal of any unauthorised development.

“The council was not aware, prior to Thursday 2 April, that the land would be used in this way.

“The site appears to be owned by those occupying the site.



“A planning application has been submitted but this is not capable of being validated at the current time.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We will continue to engage with the local community and will provide updates on the next steps when we are able to.”

News.title: Brit lawyer, 28, died days after BBL and lipo surgery in Turkey amid ‘pressure to look slim in legal profession’
News.content:
OP TRAGEDY Brit lawyer, 28, died days after BBL and lipo surgery in Turkey amid ‘pressure to look slim in legal profession’

A BRIT lawyer died days after undergoing a Brazilian butt lift and liposuction surgery at a clinic in Turkey amid “pressure to look slim in the legal profession”, an inquest heard.

Diarra Brown, 28, took out a £10,000 loan to pay for the operations at the Private Memorial Hospital in, Bahcelievler.



Black Country Coroners’ Court was told how she wanted to get her confidence back after a series of weight loss operations, which saw her drop eight dress sizes from a size 18 to size 10.



But just hours after the surgery on October 22, 2021, Diarra, of Wolverhampton, began to feel cold and complained she was sore, bruised and in severe pain.

Dr Sevket Gokham Bayam, who carried out the op, and his team told the family this was normal following surgery and it would eventually pass.

Over the weekend, Diarra’s condition deteriorated and her mum Daisy Brown contacted the hospital staff on multiple occasions but was told everything was normal.

She tragically died three days after the procedure, with the most likely cause of death given as sepsis.



Daisy told the inquest: “Before she had the bariatric surgery, she felt there was a pressure to be slim in the legal profession.

“During her training, she was still overweight and I think she got teased about it at her work.

“I don’t know what point she started talking to surgeons about the liposuction.

“I know she started talking to one surgeon in Turkey about doing all the surgery at the same time, and he said he could.



“The surgeon reassured Diarra that it would be safe.

“She spoke to the surgeon on WhatsApp before travelling to Turkey.

“She mentioned that this would be the last step in her weight loss journey and she didn’t want anything else after this.”

Diarra and her mother flew to Turkey on October 20, 2021, after being reassured the operation was possible.

Daisy said medics carried out a number of exams including blood tests and covid tests.



She continued: “Diarra had asked the surgeon if it was safe to be under anaesthetic for over five hours, he said it was. He said he had never lost a patient.”

The inquest heard Diarra soon began to suffer severe symptoms after going under the knife but was told this was normal.

She complained she could not see as she was in so much pain and could not move as her feet were so swollen but was told to walk around the room regularly.

Daisy told the inquest: “At one point Diarra told me she had wet herself and she was upset.

“When we got the taxi Diarra could not wear her seatbelt as she was on all fours because of the pain she was in.



“Diarra could not walk, she was sweating and had a high temp, was breathless and lethargic and she was in and out of consciousness.

“Her eyes kept rolling back. She was aware she was losing consciousness and told me to slap her.”

The mum said Dr Bayhan reassured her and told her to go back to the hotel while they kept Diarra in overnight but her condition worsened and she had a suspected cardiac arrest.

She tragically passed away in Turkey on October 26, 2021 – four days after the operation.

Dr Vanya Gant, a consultant in clinical microbiology and infectious diseases at University College London Hospitals, examined Diarra’s medical data and post mortem.



He concluded that Diarra went into uncontrolled septic shock.

Giving evidence, Dr Gant said: “Diarra Brown was a healthy young lady who went to Turkey.

“She suffered a disastrous and very rapid and complete collapse.

“One of the causes was uncontrolled sepsis and septic shock.

“Essentially Diarra Brown came back into hospital very fatigued. She had significant hypertension.



“She had an elevated C protein. Her white blood cell count collapsed and this happens in sepsis.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Her doctor’s description of how she was and how her mothers description was, is entirely consistent of sepsis.”

The inquest continues.

News.title: Furious driver savages Reform MP Lee Anderson - 'you put flags before potholes'
News.content:
Furious driver savages Reform MP Lee Anderson - 'you put flags before potholes'

A raging driver sabotaged Reform UK's Lee Anderson petrol station stunt in Nottinghamshire and told the 59-year-old MP to "stick his flags where the sun doesn't shine"

Reform's Lee Anderson SAVAGED by passer-by while campaigning in Nottinghamshire petrol station 720P

Reform's Lee Anderson was savaged by a furious driver who told the MP "the flags went up before the potholes were sorted", at the petrol pumps.

‌



Mr Anderson was labelled a "scumbag" as the MP tried to pull an election stunt at a petrol station in Lowdham, Nottinghamshire. The MP was approached by an unnamed woman as Mr Anderson and Tory defector Robert Jenrick launched a promotion to sell petrol to locals for cheaper.

‌



During the party event, Mr Anderson and Mr Jenrick "cut" fuel prices by 13p per litre at a Gulf petrol station in the Midlands. However, Mr Anderson, 59, was heckled by the driver who said: "You could not tell the truth if your life depended on it."

‌



View 3 Images An angry driver confronted Reform's Lee Anderson at the pumps (Image: The Mirror/YouTube)

Reform activist visited by Farage wrote vile Hitler posts - so we confronted him READ MORE :

The driver confronted the politician - who is the MP for the nearby constituency of Ashfield - about the state of the roads. The woman said: "The flags went up before the potholes were sorted." She added: "So get your silly little racist flags and stick them where the sun doesn't shine. Pathetic."

As the driver walked away, Mr Anderson smiled and replied: "Nice to meet you, have a lovely day." Mr Anderson then turned back to the driver and claimed the potholes in his constituency had been fixed.

‌



He said: "Come to Ashfield, you can see the potholes been mended." The furious woman replied: "I used to teach in Ashfield actually and it's appalling." The driver then called Mr Anderson a "scumbag" as she walked off.

View 3 Images A furious driver labelled Lee Anderson a 'scumbag' (Image: The Mirror/YouTube)

The Reform Party has been holding events across the UK to draw attention to their plans to cut VAT on fuel from 20% to 10%. The party has claimed this would lead to lower prices at the pumps.

‌



Controversy across the nation erupted last summer between residents and several councils over St George's cross flags. Flags were put up during the Lioness' Euros campaign in July.

Despite this, a group calling themselves the Weoley Warriors claimed responsibility for putting up thousands of flags on lampposts and other areas in southwest Birmingham.

View 3 Images Lee Anderson and Robert Jenrick at a Gulf petrol station in Lowdham, Nottinghamshire (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

‌



The group, in a fundraiser, claimed they were a "group of proud English men with a common goal to show Birmingham and the rest of the country of how proud we are of our history, freedoms and achievements".

More flags were spotted across the country, included the cross being painted on zebra crossings and roundabouts. At the time, advocacy group HopenotHate claimed that some of those linked to the activism are hardened and extreme far-right activists. Britain First claimed to have provided many of the flags in the North West.

In summer, a spokesperson for HopenotHate said: "There is nothing wrong with raising the Union Jack or cross of St George. Despite what people claim on social media, it’s not illegal to be proud to be English or British! It’s also true that not everyone who has raised a flag is far right.

Article continues below

"But the fact that much of this wave of activism is being organised by well-known racists and extremists does raise questions about the motivations behind much of Operation Raise the Colours." Downing Street, in summer, said the Prime Minister was "absolutely" supportive of people who put up English flags.

News.title: England fans face sevenfold New York price increase in latest World Cup rip off
News.content:
England fans face sevenfold New York price increase in latest World Cup rip off

England fans will descend on New Jersey's MetLife Stadium in July at the World Cup but a return rail ticket will cost them significantly more than the usual price

View 2 Images MetLife Stadium will host the 2026 World Cup final (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA)

Fans attending the World Cup in the United States this summer will be forced to cough up a staggering $100 (£73.69) for a return rail ticket from New York's Pennsylvania station to MetLife Stadium.

‌



The impressive 82,500 capacity venue, home to the New York Giants and New York Mets, will host eight games at this summer's World Cup, including the final on July 19 and England's final group game against Panama. But unfortunately for supporters planning to attend a fixture in New Jersey, a rail ticket will cost over seven times more than it did during the Club World Cup final last summer.

‌



That is per a new report from The Athletic, who reveal that NJ Transit, New Jersey’s transportation provider, are planning to charge fans significantly more than the $12.90 (£9.51) the 18-mile journey usually costs for a return ticket.

‌



New special event pricing will come into effect for the tournament with a final decision on costs said to be made in the coming day, the report adds.

Napoli chief proposes host of rule changes including reducing matches to 50 minutes READ MORE :

FIFA to ask Donald Trump to freeze ICE raids at World Cup as discussions come to light READ MORE :

A spokesperson for NJ Transit told the outlet: “The ticket prices for match day travel have not been finalized and any reference to cost would be unconfirmed speculation.”

“However, as the Governor clearly stated at an earlier press conference this morning with NJ Transit, the cost for the eight matches will not be borne by our regular commuters.”

‌



View 2 Images The World Cup takes place in the USA, Canada and Mexico this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Tens of thousands of fans are likely to be affected with parking at MetLife Stadium expected to be significantly reduced compared to games involving the Giants and the Mets.

New Jersey are not the only state to significantly increase travel prices ahead of the 2026 tournament, which will be hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, with Boston confirming they will charge passengers $80 (£58.97) to get to Foxboro’s Gillette Stadium - four times the usual $20 (£14.74) return.

News.title: John Cleese returns to Torquay for first time since encountering real Basil Fawlty 50 years ago
News.content:
John Cleese returns to Torquay for first time since encountering real Basil Fawlty 50 years ago

Fawlty Towers legend John Cleese has returned to Torquay for the first time in over 50 years as the hit West End play tours to the town where it all began

John Cleese returns to Torquay

Fawlty Towers legend John Cleese has returned to Torquay for the first time in more than 50 years - and the infamous incident that led to the creation of the comedy classic. The star, now 86, was last in the seaside town experiencing the 'astonishing' rudeness of the hotelier Donald Sinclair in 1971 - an encounter that inspired Basil Fawlty.

‌



But in an interview today (Tuesday, April 14), looking over the town's harbour, he said it felt like bringing the show home as he recalled the encounter at the now-demolished Gleneagles hotel that led to its creation.

‌



John was at the Princess Theatre as the Fawlty Towers play, a hit West End show now on tour, came to town. He said: "It has been a long time since I was in Torquay but it is lovely to be back. I used to come here a lot in the mid-50s, because my closest friend lived here and we used to spend long summers playing miniature golf.

‌



"Then I came back in the 70s when Python came to film here. Most of them left the Gleneagles Hotel after 24 hours to go to the Imperial. I stayed on and thank god I did as it gave me lots of items.

"Then I came back to the show the hotel to the producers and to our disappointment Mr Sinclair had left and gone to Miami. I was met by a nice agreeable chap, which was a great disappointment."

View 2 Images John Cleese on Princess Pier in Torquay (Image: SWNS)

‌



Recalling his encounter with Mr Sinclair, John added: "When I arrived to the Gleneagles I remember it seemed strange. I walked in and there was this guy sitting at a reception desk, staring into space, not doing anything - and the moment he saw me he looked busy, turned his back on me. I walked over to the reception desk and I thought what's going on? - he knows I am there.

"So after a time I went mmmm, and he said, 'oh what?', which is an extraordinary thing that someone in the hotel business, which is all about hospitality and making people feel welcome. His attitude to the guests where they were pests and they were the ones stopping him running the hotel properly.

"I stayed on with Connie, my wife, probably out of laziness, I can not think of another good reason."

‌



John said the idea for Fawlty Towers didn't come to him for a long time after the encounter in 1971. He added: "I left Python in 73 and then in 74 and was asked what I now wanted to do. I said I wanted to do something with my wife as we laugh a lot together.

"The BBC were wonderful in those days. We went away to talk about it and she said 'what about that hotel'? I said, great idea, and the BBC commissioned it. It is a shame the Gleneagles got demolished but there was nothing of that hotel in the actual show. All exterior was shot elsewhere.

"Although he had left, a newspaper tracked him down to Miami and spoke to his daughter, who never watched the tv show. She had left England before it started so the journalist asked her watch a couple of episodes. After she had, she turned to the journalist and just said, 'yeah, that is dad'."

‌



The show is beginning a run at the Princess Theatre and John is planning to address the crowd tonight. He added: "I was hoping it would come back here to Torquay at some point. It has been on a very big tour and ran a long time in the west end.

"It is getting really wonderful receptions as it is good old fashioned British farce. You don't see it very much anymore. I am abroad a lot and when I come back and ask is there been anything funny on telly - the answer is almost always not.

"We used to have so many good shows. The Good Life, Yes Minister, Only Fools, Blackadder. Now we don't have any. I have tried to figure out why it is. But I can only conclude the BBC in charge of comedy don't know how to nurture comedy.

‌



"Basil would have struggled with the modern world, I struggle hard with the modern world. There has been a huge advance in technology but has it actually made anyone any happier? When people answer that it undermines a lot of what people say.

"I have loved seeing the show sat in my little box and watching the audience laugh. People get so much friendlier when they laugh. It is not just a haha - but people doubling up like that. It is wonderful and joyous to watch."

View 2 Images It is the first time John has been back in Torquay in more than 50 years (Image: SWNS)

‌



John said at the beginning it was all fans of the show attending the musical with an average age of 70. But now kids who had never even heard of the show are embracing the 'straightforward farce and human behaviour."

He said he was 'genuinely astonished' at the quality of three Basils during the original audition and picked Adam Jackson-Smith "as he looked like me."

He said the current Basil, Danny Bayne plays the role a little differently but was a 'wonderful funny actor'. He added: "There is a very affectionate feeling in the group. They all like each other and comedy can only happen when people do.

Article continues below

"I make some suggestions on how to play Basil and changed a few things that people don't know as I've been doing it for 60 years. I might just suggest to change the order and make something immediately funnier. I think it's just an instinctive thing.

"I got here last night and had a wonderful dinner. And I think tonight we are going to be the happiest group of people in England. It is just wonderful.

"The response from people everywhere has been great. Torquay has always been so closely linked to the show and I understand Torquay has always treated it with affection. I gather from talking to people here they are fond of the show and like the fact it has made Torquay famous. In America no-one knew about it - but now they all do. That is lovely."

News.title: Sarah Ferguson mystery as 'no one - including her daughters - knows where she is'
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson mystery as 'no one - including her daughters - knows where she is'

Sarah Ferguson, who was known as the Duchess of York until recently, has effectively retreated from the public eye since she and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor left the Royal Lodge

View 2 Images Little is known about Sarah Ferguson's whereabouts (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

Senior members of the Royal Family - including Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie - are unaware of Sarah Ferguson's whereabouts, it is claimed.

‌



Sources understand Beatrice and Eugenie "do not know the full picture" about their mother's location, which has become a mystery in the public eye since she and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor were booted out of the Royal Lodge in February. Andrew eventually moved to Marsh Farm, a residence on the Sandringham Estate, despite allegedly implying the property was "beneath him".

‌



But little is known about Sarah's latest move, on the other hand, reportedly even among her family members. Rob Shuter, a royal journalist, quoted a source in his latest Substack, who said: "No one knows exactly where she is…And that includes the very top... There’s real uncertainty about how much Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie know….They may not have the full picture either."

‌



The piece on the Naughty But Nice Substack adds to the discussion around Sarah's location, as her last public appearance was at the funeral of Katharine, Duchess of Kent, in September last year.

View 2 Images Sarah Ferguson took her daughters to lunch with Jeffrey Epstein in Miami (Image: Getty)

‌



We reported this month how Fergie, 66, reportedly feels "incredibly betrayed" by members of the Royal Family amid the Jeffrey Epstein scandal. The former duchess of York, 66, has faced intense criticism for her past association with the convicted sex offender.

She and her former husband Andrew, also 66, were mentioned several times in the latest releases of the files, and in emails to the sex fiend, Ms Ferguson called him her "dear spectacular and special friend". Andrew himself denies any wrongdoing.

Mr Shuter, though, believes the public will soon become aware of Sarah's whereabouts as she is likely to be planning a comeback with new projects. The source continued: "She’s not someone who disappears for good…She always comes back.... She’s thinking about a comeback. She’ll resurface, and when she does, it will be on her terms."

Article continues below

But speaking earlier this month, another source told of Fergie's feelings of "isolation". They said: "Sarah feels incredibly betrayed... Fergie’s very bitter, she’s angry and feels wronged by everyone in the family." They added, though, they believe the author is too polite to confront anyone.

Fergie, who divorced Andrew in 1996, was not offered a royal residence when she and the former Navy pilot left Royal Lodge. Since Andrew's move to Sandringham, public sightings of him have been few and far between. He's cut a lonely figure since being booted out of Royal Lodge, holing himself up at Wood Farm, and only being seen on the occasional drive or dog walk.

News.title: Mum 'died a hero' and pushed daughter's pram to safety before crane killed her
News.content:
Mum 'died a hero' and pushed daughter's pram to safety before crane killed her

Rebecca Ableman, 30, 'died a hero' as she pushed her daughter's pushchair before the crane on Kevin Miller's passing lorry struck and killed her - Miller has now been jailed

View 4 Images Rebecca Ableman saved her daughter Autumn in her final act (Image: Chris Tuczemskyi/ SWNS)

A mum "died a hero" after pushing her daughter's pram to safety before a crane on a passing lorry struck and killed her, a court heard.

‌



Lorry driver Kevin Miller has been jailed for 13 months for causing the death by careless driving of Rebecca Ableman, who was struck on the head by part of his vehicle’s loader crane.

‌



Ms Ableman, 30, had been out shopping at a local farm shop before she was struck on the head from behind by the grab of Miller’s lorry in Willingham, Cambridgeshire in 2022.

‌



William Carter, prosecuting, told Peterborough Crown Court that the boom on 71-year-old Miller’s loader crane “slew” to the nearside as he drove through the village.

View 4 Images Kevin Miller has been jailed (Image: PA)

He said the grab struck Ms Ableman “in the head from behind”, adding: “She suffered catastrophic head and brain injuries from which she died on October 16 2022.

‌



“The prosecution case is that it was his failure adequately to secure the boom of his loader crane that amounted to carelessness in this case.” Miller pleaded guilty to causing death by careless driving at an earlier hearing.

Mr Carter said that on the day of the incident, September 22 2022, Miller had set out from his depot in King’s Lynn at around 3.40am and travelled to a Network Rail yard in Leigh on Sea in Essex. He collected “about 18 tonnes of scrap metal in the form of disused railway track” and travelled through Willingham on his journey back.

View 4 Images Ms Ableman 'died a hero' (Image: PA)

‌



Mr Carter said the speed limit of the B1050 where the incident happened was 30mph, and Miller’s tachograph indicated he had been travelling at about that speed. “Mr Miller drove on apparently completely unaware that anything untoward had happened,” said Mr Carter.

He said Miller stopped at the roadside further on and used the crane controls to move the crane back to the middle of the lorry mechanically. He told police in a later interview he had “become aware as he had seen it in his mirrors that the grab had moved over to the side of his trailer”.

He had continued back to King’s Lynn, stopping in the town of March on the way to unload scrap metal. Police identified the lorry involved in the collision and got to the yard in King’s Lynn at just before 2pm.

‌



View 4 Images Miller told officers 'what’s happened mate? I ain’t hit no-one mate' (Image: James Linsell Clark / SWNS)

Miller, of Gayton Road, King’s Lynn, Norfolk, told officers “what’s happened mate? I ain’t hit no-one mate”, Mr Carter said. The prosecutor said: “He had not taken what the Crown submit was an elementary precaution of strapping the crane boom down separately.” He added: “All that was required was further strapping which can very easily be thrown over the boom and then tightened.”

Judge Matthew Lowe, sentencing, said: “To have secured the crane unit would have been the work of moments... This tragedy could have so easily been avoided but it wasn’t through the failure of this defendant to take the most basic and elementary of steps.”

‌



He said Miller “assumed the crane hydraulics would be sufficient to prevent movement as it pinched the load”. The judge said the defendant “assumed the load itself wouldn’t shift in transit” but the grabber unit moved to protrude over the nearside edge of the trailer.

“This first happened a relatively short distance and time before the grabber collided with Rebecca,” he said. He said Ms Ableman was on the pavement pushing her daughter Autumn in a pram.

“There’s no suggestion Mr Miller knew of the collision until significantly later,” he said. “He did become aware shortly later that the grabber had moved... He pulled over to use the controls for the grabber unit to put it back in place.”

‌



He sentenced Miller to 13 months in prison, of which he will serve no more than half before he is released. The judge banned Miller from driving for two years, with an extension of six and a half months to cover the time he is in prison. Miller looked straight ahead and appeared to take a deep breath as his sentence was read out.

Russell Ableman described his daughter Rebecca as a “fantastic mother” to her young daughter in a victim impact statement read to the court by the prosecutor. He said that her final act was to protect her daughter, adding that she “saved” her and “died a hero”.

Mr Ableman described his daughter as a “dedicated NHS healthcare assistant who would go the extra mile to help others”. He said that she “made everyone around her feel seen and loved”.

Article continues below

In a statement to the court, her sister Natalie Rumbold wrote: “Her last act on this earth was to push the pram away, taking the full force of the impact to save her child.”

John Dye, mitigating for Miller, said it was an “unfathomable tragedy”. “This is a man who’s devastated at the harm he’s caused,” he added.

He said Miller “had been doing this (using the grabber unit in the way he did) for 40 years” and described the incident as a “freak accident”. He said that nobody from the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) “had ever pointed out he was doing it wrong”.

News.title: 'Queen of Peak TV' Elisabeth Moss says being a parent is hardest job in the world
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'Queen of Peak TV' Elisabeth Moss says being a parent is hardest job in the world

The Handmaid's Tale star Elisabeth Moss is now playing Mary in the Apple TV series Imperfect Women, a psychological thriller series, adapted from the Araminta Hall novel

View 6 Images Actress Elisabeth Moss agrees that The West Wing is probably the greatest political drama ever made, she says of being part of the cast: “It was such a gift." (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

Stellar performances since the age of 17, when she joined a cast of established stars in The West Wing, have earned Elisabeth Moss the nickname ‘Queen of Peak TV’. Yet, the mum-of-one lavishes praise not on great actors, but on great parents. She says: “I have so much admiration for how hard not just mums, but dads, too, work.”

‌



Elisabeth, 43, is speaking about her latest role playing Mary in the Apple TV series Imperfect Women, a psychological thriller series, adapted from the Araminta Hall novel. The eight-episode show, which is currently streaming, focuses on three best friends-of-25 years - Mary, Nancy, played by Kate Mara, and Eleanor (Kerry Washington). Their lives are turned upside down when wealthy Nancy is murdered and Mary and Eleanor’s friendship begins to unravel.

‌



Elisabeth, who is also executive producer on the show, says of her character: “She’s more of a homemaker - a mum, a wife and that’s her job. And taking care of her family is everything. I have a lot of admiration for that. I think that is the hardest job in the world.” Elisabeth, who has never revealed the name or sex of her child, born in 2024, or the identity of the father - although she was reputed to have taken her baby on set when she filmed the sixth series of The Handmaid’s Tale - adds: “She [Mary] has three, so, it’s something!”

‌



View 6 Images Elisabeth Moss in a scene from Imperfect Women (Image: Copyrighted)

In the ‘whodunit-style’ thriller, as secrets and betrayals emerge, the investigation focuses on Nancy’s secret affair with a mysterious man named David. As the friends’ lives are examined and the different paths they have followed are scrutinised, Elisabeth says: “I think it’s very true to life and that part’s probably the most relatable part.”

Reflecting on the main theme of the murder, she laughs: “I hope that none of the other parts are relatable to you and your friends or anyone’s friends. But that is the thing that I related to very much.” Elisabeth’s own friendships in some ways mirror Mary’s at the start of the series. She says: “I have three best friends and one of them actually lives here in the UK. “Your lives go in different directions and, hopefully, you stay in touch. Usually, if they’re your best friend, you do. But, sometimes, you don’t even talk every day and sometimes you end up doing different things than when you were 20.

‌



“But if it really is a true best friend, you know how it is, you can not have seen them for months and then you pick up right where you left off and it’s beautiful. These three friends have that. But Mary’s life, yes, ends up being very different to Nancy and Eleanor’s.”

View 6 Images Kerry Washington, Elisabeth Moss and Kate Mara attend Today At Apple - Spotlight: The Cast & Creator Of "Imperfect Women" at Apple The Grove on March 11, 2026 in Los Angeles, California (Image: Apple TV via Getty Images)

Elisabeth, who lived in Richmond, south west London, for several years, is now settled in Sonoma, California, with her child. Married to Saturday Night Live star Fred Armisen from 2009 to 2011, she has not publicly announced a new partner, but is fiercely protective about her private life,

‌



Raised as a Scientologist by her musician parents Ron - an Englishman from Birmingham - and Linda Moss, an American, her first screen role was in 1990 when, aged six, she played Lucky Santangelo in the TV miniseries Lucky Chances. But the role that made her name was playing Zoey Bartlett, the youngest daughter of President Bartlett (Martin Sheen) in The West Wing - which she landed, aged 17.

Agreeing that The West Wing is probably the greatest political drama ever made, she says of being part of the cast: “It was such a gift. Honestly, I was 17 to 23 when I did it. I literally did my last episode of The West Wing at the beginning of April and shot the Mad Men pilot at the end of April.

6 View 6 Images Elisabeth Moss with her husband Fred Armisen (Image: WireImage) 6 View 6 Images Elisabeth Moss attends the UK photocall for Hulu's "The Testaments", coming to Disney+ on 8th of April, at Raffles London at The OWO on March 23, 2026 in London, England (Image: Grant Buchanan/Dave Benett/Getty Images for Disney+)

‌



“I am very, very fortunate. The coolest thing was the people I got to work with. Looking back…at the time I appreciated it…but now, I’m like ‘oh my god I was 17 and was with Bradly Whitford, Martin Sheen, Richard Schiff, Alison Janney, John Spencer. I was with these actors that are just some of the best that we have - learning from them. And not just on camera, but off camera.”

Elisabeth, who went on to play Peggy Olsen - working for the troubled advertising genius Don Draper (Jon Hamm) in Mad Men - says The West Wing also taught her how to behave towards her colleagues. She says: “That is where I learned how to be on set. That is where I learned how you are supposed to behave; how you’re supposed to treat other people; how you’re supposed to collaborate with the crew. Martin Sheen would, literally, treat the background actor who was there exactly the same way as he would treat the other lead actor in the scene. And I was like ‘that’s how you’re supposed to be.’ So, it was an incredible learning experience.”

Elisabeth, who has also starred in movies including The Invisible Man and The One I Love, as well as being awarded a Tony for her role on Broadway in The Heidi Chronicles, cites The Handmaid’s Tale - adapted from Margaret Attwood’s novel - as the role that changed her life. Set in a dystopian society, she plays June Osborne, of whom she says: “I find her very inspiring. I find her just so cool and strong and complicated. I’ve always been kind of inspired by June. Again, just a gift to portray somebody who I look up to.”

‌



View 6 Images Offred played by Elisabeth Moss in the Handmaid's Tale (Image: Hulu)

The main star of the series, she adds: “It was a very life changing experience personally and professionally for me. Nine years doing that. And I learned how to be a producer, I learned how to be a director, I really learned how to lead a show, as well as my first time being number one on the call sheet. It was really a big, life changing experience.”

Returning to the present, she confesses that she was attracted by the structure of Arminta Hall’s Imperfect Women. She says: “It was really the structure of the book that starts with Kerry’s character, Eleanor, and then goes to Kate’s character, Nancy, and then mine. There was also a lot of fun, delicious, juicy stuff in the book and the show.”

Article continues below

But she confesses that it was sheer chance that the series was ever made. She says: “It’s a brilliant book that I truly fell in love with. I bought it at the airport because I loved the cover and the title. I’m very deep that way!”

*This interview was adapted from The Arts Hour on the BBC World Service and is available on BBC Sounds.

News.title: Reform activist visited by Farage wrote vile Hitler posts - so we confronted him
News.content:
A Reform local elections campaigner whose tanning salon was visited by Nigel Farage praised Adolf Hitler, we can reveal.

Aaron Taylor, who was planning to be a candidate and served as a branch treasurer, shared a tribute to the Nazi dictator. The 33-year-old, also pictured with Reform’s Robert Jenrick, even wrote “heil Hitler” online and denied the Holocaust. Taylor, who has been enthusiastically campaigning in recent weeks, posted images in January showing the party’s leader visiting his Sun Spa salon in Essex. Only months earlier he shared a picture of Hitler online emblazoned with the message: “I gave it my all. Now its [sic] time, for you to give it your all”.

View 5 Images Mirror reporter Simon Murphy presents evidence to Taylor at his tanning salon (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

The now deleted tweet in late October was posted in response to an X user who complained about their feed being “anti Jews and anti Israel ”. And, in another tweet the same month, Taylor wrote: “The greatest deception of all time is that the nazis we’re [sic] evil and the holocaust was real… it would seem.” The posts were uncovered by anti-racism campaign group HOPE Not Hate (HNH).

‌



Today we confronted Taylor at his salon in Jaywick, in Farage’s Clacton constituency, where he said sorry. Taylor, who explained he had been “removed” from the party, said : “I genuinely apologise.” He added: “I got pulled up on it. I don’t remember posting these things… it’s likely I’ve had a beer, said stupid things.”

It comes as Reform has been riding high in the polls, with Farage seeking to use May 7th’s ballot as a referendum on PM Keir Starmer ’s popularity. HNH’s director of research Joe Mulhall said: “We have become used to finding extreme and unacceptable Reform activists. But to see such open support for Hitler and brazen Holocaust denial from a Reform campaigner is still shocking. The party has no option but to expel people like Taylor but the question remains why someone so extreme feels that Reform is the party for them?”

View 5 Images Taylor's sickening post last year paying tribute to Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler

Taylor – who calls Farage “the big boss” – is an avid campaigner on X, billing himself as a “proud” member and volunteer for Reform. In a video pinned to the top of his profile, he stands outside Parliament donning a tie boasting about volunteering at the party’s HQ. “I can’t wait for the local elections on May 7th,” he tells viewers before pointing his finger to the camera as he adds: “Let’s get on it.”

‌



But this polished image is a far cry from the extreme posts he shared. Until last month, Taylor’s Twitter account went under the name “@the_jackal123” before being changed to “AaronEssexTay”. In now deleted posts, Taylor repeatedly demonstrated his support for Hitler. On October 25, he wrote: “Listen to the translations of Adolf Hitler and compare to the world we live in now currently. The winners of the war lied about how evil Hitler was it would seem.. interesting”.

And, in an apparent reference to the Führer, the same day he wrote: “The Austrian painter was right”. Responding to another account’s suggestion that people dress up in Nazi costumes for Halloween and “troll our government”, Taylor wrote the next day: “HEIL HITLER”. On November 1, he continued a sickening racist rant.

View 5 Images We confronted Taylor at his salon in Jaywick, in Farage’s Clacton constituency, where he said sorry (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

Meanwhile, in a post which was still available on his account today, Taylor shared a ‘white pride’ video featuring Hitler’s propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels. Taylor reposted the white pride video and accompanying tweet from October which said: “You’re blessed to be white. Be proud of it.” As recently as March 10 Taylor crowed about being at the Reform’s HQ. That day he posted a picture smiling with Treasury spokesman Jenrick who defected from the Tories earlier this year. And, in February, he shared a picture shaking hands with Reform’s home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf.

‌



Taylor’s X profile previously said he was treasurer for Harwich and north Essex’s Reform UK branch. He is director of Sun Spa 11 Ltd. Last week, the firm was offering customers a cash-only “FIVER FRIDAY” deal of “10 mins tanning” for £5. In January, Taylor shared images of Farage visiting the salon.

Asked about his campaigning for Reform, Taylor said: “I’ve been removed.” He confirmed he had been treasurer for the party’s Harwich branch but stopped doing the role “about a month ago”, adding: “They disagreed with something I said… a year before I was a member.”

View 5 Images Taylor poses with Reform UK's treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick

Asked about why he tweeted in support of Hitler, Taylor said: “I don’t remember doing it, to be honest,” laughing. Questioned on whether he was asked to be a candidate, he said: “Candidate and ‘we need a treasurer, do you want to do it?’ I said yeah, that’s fine.” Taylor said he cancelled his membership, claiming he had not been expelled.

‌



He confirmed he visited Reform HQ last month, adding: “A day or two after that I got pulled up for comments.” Asked if they were the Hitler comments, he replied: “Probably.” We presented him with a dossier of HNH’s evidence showing his tweets, including claiming “the winners of the war lied about how evil Hitler was”. He said he did not stand by the comment. Pointed out he had posted a vile racist tweet and asked why, he said: “I don’t remember doing that, to be honest. I don’t believe that.”

Reform said: “Mr Taylor is not a member of Reform UK and was rejected as a candidate for the party.” A source said Taylor applied to be a candidate but failed vetting and that he served as an interim branch treasurer for six weeks.

News.title: Brits battle to for £1billion prize in new lottery bonanza - but there's a catch
News.content:
Brits battle to for £1billion prize in new lottery bonanza - but there's a catch

The National Lottery, operated by Allwyn, will launch a new draw which will link with the famous Powerball game, iconic in the US, in which the jackpot can rocket

View 2 Images Allwyn runs the National Lottery games in the UK

Brits could be in with a chance of scooping a mind-boggling £1billion lottery bonanza under plans announced today.

‌



New National Lottery operator Allwyn confirmed it will launch a new draw later this year that links up with America’s famous Powerball game.

‌



The draw - which takes places three times a week - will offer the chance to win a truly life-changing amount, from at least £12million. Unlike other draws, there is no limit to the number of roll-overs that can take place if no-one wins, meaning the jackpot can soar. Allwyn says it paves the way for one lucky person in the UK to win a colossal £1billion, or more - the biggest such prize every offered.

‌



But unlike most other National Lottery winners who get their hands on the tax-free cash at once, those who scoop the top Powerball prize have to receive it over a 30-year period. For those who net the potential £1billion, it would work out at more than £30million every year for three decades. Should the lucky winner sadly not live that long, the remainder will be paid to their estate, an Allwyn spokeswoman said.

Woman told to return £33k jackpot after William Hill claims technical glitch READ MORE :

View 2 Images The US Powerball jackpot reached a staggering $950million last year in the US (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

But before players get too carried away, the odds of winning the Powerball jackpot are a distinctly distance 292 million to one, given the fact there will be up against others in 48 US state lotteries. And it is not cheap, at £4 per Powerball line - the most expensive National Lottery draw in the game’s history.

‌



That is much more than the $2 in the States - something Allwyn says it due to there being more lower tier prizes in the UK. For instance, matching two main numbers wins a fixed prize of £8, rising to £1million for having five main numbers.

The exact date of the launch has yet to be confirmed but UK Powerball players will pick five main numbers ranging from numbers from 1 to 69, and one Powerball number from 1 to 26. Or they can choose a Lucky Dip.

Tickets will be available to buy online or in store by 11.55pm the night before the draws (on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays), with the draws then happening around 4am the next morning – on Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday – from the Powerball studio in Florida.

‌



The biggest ever Powerball winner was Edwin Castro, who netted just over $2billion on the California state lottery in November 2022. However, the 31-year-old opted to take it in one go - rather over several decades - which brought the cash prize down to just under $1billion, after tax, still an astonishing amount.

Castro - who bought his lucky ticket at a fuel station - reportedly used his record-breaking winnings to buy himself a luxury £18million home for himself in the Hollywood Hills, another £3million Japanese-inspired pad for his parents, along with various sports cars and exotic trips.

His hometown of Altadena, which is a 20-minute drive from Los Angeles, was severely impacted by wildfires last year, which killed at least 31 people and laid waste to a staggering 57,000 acres as fires ripped their way through local neighbourhoods. He reportedly bought up 15 lots plots of land in Altadenato the tune of $10m about £7,500,000. Speaking to The Wall Street Journal, he said: "I want it to feel like the old neighbourhood. Like if you put all those houses pre-fire in a time bubble."

‌



The UK’s inclusion is first time the Powerball game has taken place outside the US, and builds on the launch of the pan-European Euromillions draw in 2004.

The move comes as Allwyn also announced a big change to the main Lotto draw, in the biggest chance since its launch in 1994.

From June 7, every £2 Lotto line will give players two chances to win – with the same number of balls to choose from and a new two-round format every draw.

‌

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes has delivered a stark assessment of the Premier League title race, declaring that “Arsenal are gone” and asserting that “all the momentum” lies with Manchester City.

The Gunners’ lead at the top was cut to six points at the weekend after they suffered a shock 2-1 defeat at home to Bournemouth while City claimed an emphatic 3-0 win at Chelsea.

City, who have played one game less than Arsenal, can eat further into the deficit when the top two meet in a mouthwatering showdown at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

And Scholes, who won 11 top-flight titles during a glittering career with Manchester United, envisions the league trophy heading back to City for the fifth time in the last six seasons.

open image in gallery Arsenal’s Gabriel looked deflated after the defeat by Bournemouth on Saturday (Adam Davy/PA) ( PA Wire )

"I just think Arsenal are gone and all of the momentum is with Manchester City," Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast.

"At some point you’ve got to beat your rivals to win the league. I’ve not seen them do it, they don’t win big games. I can’t see anything other than a City win on Sunday, I just can’t."

City underwhelmed last season as Liverpool ended their run of four straight league titles and Pep Guardiola’s side have struggled for consistency in this campaign.

However, having been eliminated from the Champions League by Real Madrid, City defeated Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final, thrashed Liverpool in their FA Cup quarter-final then put Chelsea to the sword.

"Pep has had to coach this team in the last six months more than he’s ever had to do in years and years," Scholes added. "The teams he’s had (in the past), he’s just had to sit back and watch.

"Now in this last six to 12 months, he’s had to coach them. The likes of (Jeremy) Doku and (Rayan) Cherki, he’s got to talk them through games a little bit and he’s not really done that for a while."

Former England goalkeeper Mary Earps was given a rousing reception on her appearance at the Lionesses’ World Cup qualifier against Spain at Wembley.

Earps retired from international duty last year and was attending a celebration of her career with the Lionesses before Tuesday’s game.

England manager Sarina Wiegman said before the game that she hoped Earps, who earned 53 caps and kept 26 clean sheets, would get the retirement send-off she “deserves”. The warm applause at Wembley indicated that the furore surrounding comments she made in her autobiography late last year had been forgiven if not forgotten by large numbers of fans.

Earps became England’s No 1 in 2021 and played a key role in their Euro 2022 triumph and run to the 2023 World Cup final that saw her recognised as the world’s best keeper, but opted to retire from England duty after losing her place to Hannah Hampton shortly before Euro 2025.

She went on criticise Wiegman’s decision to restore Hampton to the squad in her explosive autobiography ‘All In’, which was published in November last year.

The Paris Saint-Germain keeper has since said she learned “some tough lessons” from the book’s publication and subsequent backlash, telling The Guardian in February that there were “clearly things that I could have done better”.

She has played just once in England since her book was published, when making her return to former club Manchester United in the Women’s Champions League. On that occasion there were a smattering of boos as well as cheers.

However on Tuesday there were loud cheers as she was presented with a framed shirt marking her 53 caps, as well as a bouquet of flowers on the pitch at Wembley to celebrate her contribution to the team.

open image in gallery She was presented with a bouquet of flowers and special framed shirt ( AP )

The Euro 2022 winner also received a warm hug from Leah Williamson, Lucy Bronze, Keira Walsh and Alessia Russo, as England headed off the pitch at the end of their warm-up.

Wiegman said before Tuesday’s presentation: “It shows what she has done for the game, what she has done for England. She is an inspiration for so many people, particularly young goalkeepers. She deserves a great farewell. I hope we celebrate her and it will be a nice moment.

“I think some people have been disappointed, some people will be thinking she is inspirational, everyone will have an opinion. But let’s cherish the moments we had together. Mary had a great career and for us was the world’s best. She played important games and now she has moved on. Let’s all celebrate her.”

The FA has made efforts to honour former England players following their international retirements and there was a send-off for Euros winner Fran Kirby before the friendly against China in November, as well as former captain Steph Houghton before a friendly with Germany in October 2024.

Lonna Drewes, a fifth woman to come forward with allegations against California Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell, detailed a graphic account of sexual violence during a press conference in Beverly Hills on Tuesday.

The misconduct allegations against Swalwell were first published by The San Francisco Chronicle and CNN last Friday, prompting him to dismiss them in a social media video as “absolutely false,” insisting the incidents alleged “never happened,” and pledging to “fight them with everything that I have.”

He has since announced he is abandoning his bid for the governor’s mansion and is resigning from Congress after the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office opened an investigation into the claims against him.

Represented by attorneys Lisa Bloom and Arick Fudali, Drewes alleged that the outgoing congressman drugged and raped her in 2018. Drewes stated that after meeting Swalwell for professional networking in West Hollywood, she became incapacitated following a single glass of wine.

She described a violent assault in a hotel room, telling reporters: “He raped me and he choked me. While he was choking me, I lost consciousness and I thought I died. I did not consent to any sexual activity.”

open image in gallery California Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell has insisted the sexual abuse allegations against him are ‘absolutely false’ but has abandoned his bid for governor and announced his resignation from Congress ( AFP/Getty )

Bloom confirmed that her office was filing a formal police report with the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Office, shifting the focus of the scandal toward a criminal investigation.

The new allegations follow Swalwell’s abrupt exit from public life on Monday, April 13, when he announced his resignation from Congress and withdrew from the California gubernatorial race.

For the women who initially went public with accusations against the Democrat, Drewes’ testimony represents the “receipts” they said were forthcoming.

The three women – Cheyenne Hunt, Annika Albrecht, and Ally Sammarco – gave an interview to CBS News’ Nancy Cordes, in which they were asked whether they consider the Democrat’s sudden downfall justice.

“No, it’s just the beginning,” Hunt answered Cordes in a preview of their exchange published before broadcast. “It’s just the very beginning, and I know personally that we’re not walking away from this fight.”

“For me justice won’t be until he can’t ever harm a woman ever again and he has faced the consequences for the women that he has harmed,” said Albrecht.

“I think, in regards to the governor’s race, he never should have run for governor to begin with knowing the kind of history and receipts that are out there,” Sammarco said.

“So that’s a non-starter and then, in terms of Congress, I think he absolutely should have resigned.

“I think we just prevented another 30 to 40 years, potentially, of him harming people if he were to stay in Congress so, in that sense, I think we have served justice for his future victims that won’t exist anymore.”

Sammarco also said she felt “vindicated” by Swalwell having to respond to their accusations.

open image in gallery Ally Sammarco, Annika Albrecht, and Cheynene Hunt – who have accused Swalwell of sexual misconduct – discuss their ordeals with CBS News journalist Nancy Cordes ( CBS News )

“He was pushed into a corner, essentially, because they were planning to expel him… So I think he did that to save face a little,” she said of his resignation from the House of Representatives. “But I also felt very vindicated that he realized it was over for him.”

She and Albrecht denied any suggestion that they might have known each other before their shared ordeals were brought to light, rubbishing the idea that they might have come forward together as part of a coordinated plot to sabotage Swalwell’s gubernatorial chances.

“We didn’t know each other before,” Sammarco said. “I didn’t know any of the other women. I knew nothing about them. We got connected through this process, and I’m so glad we did.”

Albrecht explained that the process began when she reached out to Hunt, a friend and social media influencer, to ask her about posting a video of her allegations against Swalwell because, she said, she felt “physically sick and nauseous” about the prospect of him becoming California’s next governor.

“Eleven days is how long it took from when I reached out to her to make the video to when the dam broke and all the articles were published,” Albrecht said, calling them “the longest 11 days of our lives.”

open image in gallery Swalwell accuser Ally Sammarco says he should never have run for California governor 'knowing the kind of history and receipts that are out there' ( CBS News )

She said they were “immediately slammed” by messages from other women making allegations against Swalwell, many of which appeared to follow a similar pattern to their own experiences.

“He thought he was untouchable,” Sammarco said of the outgoing congressman. “He acted with total impunity. He never thought that the consequences of his actions would follow him.”

"As governor, he would have had even more power and more authority. And he would have felt vindicated too, you know, that he could run for higher office.

“He ran for president [in 2019] and nothing came out about him. So I think that empowered him to continue doing what he was doing.”

Later in the same interview, she said of Swalwell: “He gave off this perception that he was a family man. That he was a fighter. That he was a defender of women. And that couldn’t be further from the truth.

“If these are the people that are out there championing women and, you know, protectors of women, and ‘We need to hold people accountable,’ and then behind closed doors they're doing this, that is a huge discrepancy for anybody who’s working in politics.
